meta.event: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 · Lunar Landing Site Navigator

terrain.source: NASA LRO LOLA GDR polar DEMs (PDS LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0, imbrium.mit.edu)

ephemeris.observer: site on the Moon (coord@301, MEAN_ME), airless

calc_si_usage.scope: Hyunji (calculation) set the direction of this part, asked for each check (for example re-running the NHF comparison on every passing date and measuring the interpolation error), and reviewed and approved every setting. Claude (AI) drafted the Python code and carried out the analyses she requested. All reported numbers come from our own runs.

calc_references: Mazarico et al. (2011), Icarus 211, 1066-1081: LOLA polar illumination maps, NASA PGDA, https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/69

terrain.source: NASA LRO LOLA GDR polar DEMs (PDS, imbrium.mit.edu)
terrain.horizon_method: max terrain elevation angle along great circles, exact 3-D sphere geometry (curvature included); 40 m steps to 20 km, 80 m steps beyond; rays stop where the DEMs end
terrain.limits: rays end at the DEM edge (about 80S); terrain smaller than 40-80 m is not seen

ephemeris.observer: site on the Moon (coord@301, geodetic, MEAN_ME), airless
ephemeris.quantities: apparent azimuth/elevation (az from north toward east), angular diameter

rules.sun_frac: visible fraction of the solar disk above the local horizon, 0-1
rules.earth_vis: 1 if any part of Earth's disk is above the local horizon (NASA PGDA convention)

rules.approach_by_az: fraction of ground points under the descent camera, 0.5-10 km uprange of the pad, whose Sun centre is above their own horizon (seen from 1.0 m above the ground), 0-1
rules.approach: best of the 8 approach azimuths, 0-1 (pass/fail threshold comes from Keev's criteria)
rules.approach_az_deg: direction the lander flies in FROM, measured from north toward east

power_mean.source: Assumed demo threshold. NASA describes variable sunlight at the lunar south pole but does not specify a 50% minimum. https://www.nasa.gov/reference/moonbase-environment/

power_dark.source: Assumed demo threshold. NASA describes extended periods of shadow at the lunar south pole but does not specify a 96-hour maximum. https://www.nasa.gov/reference/moonbase-environment/

comm_frac.source: Assumed demo threshold. NASA describes changing Earth line-of-sight conditions but does not specify a 40% minimum. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20250003508

comm_gap.source: Assumed demo threshold. NASA describes approximately two-week cycles in south-pole communication and solar availability, not a 240-hour maximum gap. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20220010599

approach.source: Assumed demo threshold. NASA discusses lighting and communication constraints during south-pole landing approach but does not specify a 0.50 threshold. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20220010599
